description:
Inter-annotator agreement — Layer 4. Returns Cohen's κ
(n=2 raters), Fleiss' κ, Krippendorff's α, Scott's π +
Landis-Koch interpretation, plus the multi-rater coverage report.

`min_raters` overrides the ranking's configured min_raters_per_pair.

Also returns `judge_alignment` — how AI judges relate to people on
this ranking: each judge's agreement with the human majority (Cohen's
κ, Wilson 95% interval, overlap), the pairs where the focus judge
(`judge_id`, default the most prolific) and people disagree, the
escalation queue (pairs the judge could not be trusted on and the
human votes they still need) and `next_steps`. `judge_alignment.audit`
measures the focus judge on the audit slice, a random sample of the
pairs it labelled (agreement with a Wilson interval, and how much of
the slice people have answered), and gives each item's win share
corrected by people's choices there (prediction-powered inference:
`estimate`, `interval_95`, `people_only`, `sample_gain`).

`bridging` is agreement ACROSS groups of voters: each item's score
is high only if every group prefers it (Polis group-informed
consensus: the geometric mean over groups of (wins + 1) /
(comparisons + 2)), with `lowest_group_rate`, `spread` and the items
groups part on most. Groups are what voters declared on the vote;
`group_by` names the `voter_segment` key (default: the key with the
most groups of at least 5 people). With fewer than two such groups
it returns a status and a note, not a score.

For the ranking's owner it also returns `principles`: the rules
derived from people's choices (`rules_markdown`, ready to put in an
agent's instructions), each with the held-out pairs it applied to
and how often it sided with people. Derive them with
`aimrank_synthesize_judge_prompt` (`mode="principles"`).

For the ranking's owner and moderators it also returns
`contestants`: the result per maker (agent version, model, prompt).
Name each item's maker in its private `_contestant` attribute, which
voters and judges never see; each maker gets a Bradley-Terry rating
across cases with a case-resampled 95% interval, `clearly_ahead_of_next`,
and `surprises` (cases a maker lost to one rated well below it).
People (`people`) and the AI judge (`ai_judge`) are fitted apart.

api_key is optional on the public endpoint; on /mcp/mcp a missing
key is refused.
name: aimrank_get_agreement
title: Rater agreement
